meta.company: Squishable Inc (independent plush studio, est. 2007, New York)
meta.thesis: Squishable does not need more plush designs - it needs adults to admit they want one, and Hug Certified turns an impulsive squeeze into a purchase reason.

business_problem: Squishable sells joy in a box but markets like a toy company: the review base (n=125 analyzed, ~96% five-star) is tiny relative to site traffic, 'cute' and 'love' dominate while almost nobody talks about buying for themselves, and impulse purchase has no offline trigger - shoppers can't feel the squish through a screen [R1][R3][S1][S5].

objectives.text: Drive 180 attributed orders (pop-up QR + online code HUG15) in 45 days at ~$42 average order value
Capture 700 email/SMS signups via Hug Certified pop-ups and the Drop Day waitlist
Reach 900K Texas impressions and shift 'plush is for kids' perception: +10 pts on 'plush is a self-care/collectible product' among surveyed shoppers

segments.name: Comfort-Seeking Adults (18-34)
segments.psychographic: buys self-care, desk decor, comfort objects; follows squish/plush content; impulse-gifter
segments.behavioral: shops TikTok/IG trends, buys gifts online, visits pop-ups
segments.media: TikTok, Instagram, email, campus/mall foot traffic

segments.name: Gifters & Collectors
segments.behavioral: joins waitlists, buys on drop days, holiday-driven

methods.recruitment: All public Judge.me reviews on squishable.com, keyword-coded (collected 2026-11-07)
Squishable.com product/pricing pages, drop calendar, social bios vs Squishmallows/Gund positioning
Intercept survey at pop-up locations, pre vs post campaign

findings.finding: 'Cute' and 'love' dominate reviews (44 and 43 of 125 mentions) - buyers describe emotional attachment, but almost none describe a reason they bought *for themselves*
96% five-star across 125 reviews with essentially zero product complaints - the product is not the problem, discovery and self-purchase permission are
Gift mentions outnumber self-purchase mentions ~3:1; 'hug', 'squish', 'soft' appear organically - the squeeze IS the product demo, and it is entirely offline-inaccessible
Collector/drop language is nearly absent from reviews while Squishmallows built a billion-dollar brand on collector drops - the model exists, Squishable under-uses it

assumptions.text: ~$42 blended AOV (site pricing ~$15-55; mix of mini + full-size plush)
Gross margin ~55% on DTC plush (typical plush/soft goods)
$4,800 paid social/creator at ~$8 CPM = ~600K impressions + ~300K organic
6 Hug Certified pop-up days at ~$350/shift (booth, samples=small plush, signage)
HUG15 code gives $5 off $30+; manufacturer-funded, netted in revenue

programs.name: Hug Certified Stations
programs.mechanic: Pop-up comfort booths at campus/mall spots: free hug booth with a real plush wall, 'Hug Certified' sticker + squeeze counter on video, QR badge links to $5-off code.

programs.name: Drop Day
programs.mechanic: Collector drop calendar + SMS waitlist: two limited releases teased in-feed, waitlist gets 15-min early access.

programs.name: Sofa Science
programs.mechanic: TikTok/IG comfort content: squish ASMR, desk-pet office tours, 'rate my emotional support plush' creator posts - all tagged Hug Certified.

programs.name: Adopt a Squish
programs.mechanic: Donation drive: trade in a worn plush for 20% off, donated to children's shelters - PR + feel-good earned media.

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: buyers love the product (96% five-star) but almost nobody buys *for themselves* - plush reads as a kid's toy, and the squeeze that sells it can't be felt through a screen [R1][R3].
Solution: Hug Certified - pop-up hug booths, collector drops, comfort content, and a donation drive that give adults permission to buy joy.
45-day goal: 180 attributed orders, 700 captures, +10 pts on 'plush is self-care' [O1-O3].
slides.notes: The one-sentence version: we certify the hug, then sell it.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Squishable: giant round plush - cute, oversized, soft; $15-55 price ladder from minis to 15-inch+ designs. [S1]
Independent studio est. 2007 in New York; DTC site + collector drops; designs span food, animals, fantasy. [S1]
Reviews: 96% five-star - 'cute', 'soft', 'love' are the vocabulary; quality complaints essentially absent [R2].
Sold DTC online; emotional-purchase product whose demo is the squeeze itself.
slides.notes: Hold the plush while describing it - the product explains itself.

slides.title: Company & Position
bullets: Independent plush studio since 2007 - predates Squishmallows' collector model but never claimed the adult/collector positioning [S1][S4].
Squishmallows proved the market: ~$400M+/yr, adult collectors driving growth; Squishable has the product, not the positioning [S4][R4].
Current comms lean 'toy for kids/gifts' - the buyers in the reviews are adults buying comfort.
Perception gap = the campaign's opening: reposition, don't redesign.
slides.notes: The brand accidentally built an adult product and markets it to kids.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary): 180 attributed orders via HUG15 code + pop-up QR at ~$42 AOV. [O1]
O2: 700 email/SMS captures from booths + Drop Day waitlist. [O3]
O3: 900K impressions; +10 pts 'plush is self-care/collectible' on pre/post survey (n=150 + holdout). [O1]
Baseline: current list size; week-0 survey; Shopify code report. [O1]
slides.notes: Three objectives across the funnel, all measurable.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1: comfort-seeking adults 18-34 - students + young professionals who buy self-care, desk decor, and impulse comfort; TikTok/IG natives; Austin metro.
P2: gifters & collectors 25-45 - waitlist joiners, drop-day buyers, holiday-driven; DFW/Austin + online.
Both already exist in the review base - we just name and recruit them [R1].
slides.notes: P1 buys for themselves, P2 buys drops and gifts.

slides.title: Research Methodology & Results
bullets: Content analysis of 125 public Judge.me reviews (collected 2026-11-07), keyword-coded [R1-R4].
Digital shelf audit of 8 sources: product/pricing pages, drop calendar, social positioning vs Squishmallows [R4][S1].
Pending: intercept survey (n=150) at pop-up sites + 3 interviews - field kit ready.
Honest corpus limit: 125 reviews is thin; direction is consistent, magnitude approximate.
slides.notes: What we have is real; what we lack is stated plainly.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: [R1] Reviews say 'cute/love' but almost never 'bought it for myself' -> give adults a socially-acceptable reason: certification, not a toy purchase.
[R3] The squeeze sells and can't be felt online -> bring the plush to the shopper: hug booths are the conversion engine.
[R4] Drop language absent while Squishmallows monetized collectors -> Drop Day waitlist adds collector mechanics to an existing product line.
[R2] 96% five-star, zero real complaints -> we sell permission and access, not product fixes.
slides.notes: Every decision traces to a finding.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Theme: Hug Certified - the squeeze is certified, then sold.
Push-pull: pop-up booths create touch + QR (pull), retargeting + drop SMS convert later (push) [R3][A4].
Comfort repositioning, not redesign: same plush, adult framing [R1].
PESO: paid geo-social, earned shelter-donation PR, shared squish-test content, owned email/SMS waitlist.
slides.notes: One theme, four programs, all channels tagged.

slides.title: Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $10,500: paid social $4.8K [A4]; creators $3K [A6]; pop-ups $2.1K [A7]; production $600 [A10]; contingency ~14% [A11]. | O2 list value: 700 captures x ~$6 = $4.2K [O2][A13].
Funnel: 900K impressions x 2.5% CTR x 0.8% purchase = 180 orders = $7.6K revenue [A1][A4].
GP 55% = $4.2K; direct ROI ~-60% - a repositioning proof budget, not a profit play; payback via list + collectors [A2][A13].
Conservative (50%): 90 orders, ROI ~-80%; kill-trigger at week 3 protects the downside [A15].
slides.notes: Small budget, honest ROI - we sell proof, not margin.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: orders via HUG15 + QR UTMs; target 180; Shopify code report; weekly. [O3]
O2: captures; target 700; Klaviyo; weekly. [O1]
O3: impressions 900K + self-care perception +10 pts; pre/post survey w/ holdout; weekly/pre-post. [O1]
Trigger: <30 QR scans per booth day by week 3 -> shift spend to Sofa Science + Drop Day. [O1]
slides.notes: Measurement plan with kill-switch.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Squishable's product is loved; its permission structure is broken - adults buy comfort but call it a gift.
Hug Certified doesn't sell a toy; it sells the feeling and certifies it - a repositioning the team can demo live.
The booth is the presentation: put a Squishable in a judge's hands and the thesis proves itself.
slides.notes: Close on the demo - judges should still be holding it.
